interpretations.rationale: The inflated accepted index is not persisted, so a restart reloads a decision record that cannot read its own decided log, and that state precedes any recovery attempt. Receipt 33a7daae65f647c28017a29765d88faf ran restart_after_covering_sync_cannot_read_decided_log (exit 0, test passed). Event 0 records the stored fields the covering witness leaves behind: log_len 2, decided 4 and the StopSign present. Event 1 records the node rebuilt over them: accepted 3, decided 4, is_reconfigured None, read(2) as a StopSign, read(3) absent, suffix_none = 1 and suffix_len = 0. The accepted-index comparison holds as predicted. The second declared comparison is formally violated only because the harness emitted the flag as the integer 1 while the assertion names boolean true; the recorded value is the unreadable outcome and suffix_len 0 confirms nothing was returned, so that outcome is a representation mismatch rather than evidence that the decided log survived. The mechanism is the load arithmetic: decided was persisted as 4 by the clamped Decide, while accepted is recomputed as two entries plus one marker, giving 3; read_decided_suffix(0) then requests the range up to 4, get_entry_type(3) is out of bounds, and read returns None. The same recomputation moves the marker from index 3 back to index 2, clears is_reconfigured because decided no longer equals accepted, and leaves appends rejected because the stored StopSign is present. One boundary qualifies how long this lasts: the probe's storage held no promise, so the node started in Phase::None, whereas the witness node had persisted the ballot it promised and SequencePaxos::with would start such a node in Phase::Recover with a PrepareReq queued to every peer. The unreadable suffix is therefore the state at load, before those requests are answered; whether the resulting sync repairs the missing position or preserves the inconsistency is not measured here. The durable part is that the inflated state is written down as inconsistent decision metadata whose own reload cannot read the decided log.
counterevidence: A faithful restart of the witness node queues PrepareReq to every peer at construction, so the node actively seeks a fresh sequence and log sync instead of sitting with the unreadable state; the probe's passive Phase::None start does not reflect that.
The node could read its decided suffix before the restart; the loss appears only when the state is reloaded, so the defect is in the persistence boundary rather than in the running node's own reads.

The unreadability follows from decided exceeding the recomputed accepted index; a backend that persisted the accepted counter would reload differently, but the Storage trait offers no way to persist it, so the recomputation applies to every implementation.
limitations: The comparison asserting suffix_none equals true is violated by an integer/boolean mismatch in the harness; the unreadability rests on the emitted suffix_none 1 and suffix_len 0, and a corrected boolean emission would be needed for that comparison to hold formally.

The storage is populated directly with the fields the witness writes because this snapshot exposes no accessor for a live node's storage; the write path that produced them and the persisted promise are not part of this receipt.

Because no promise was stored, the rebuilt node started in Phase::None and exchanged no messages; the recovery exchange a faithful restart would initiate, and whether it repairs the missing position, is untested.
No snapshot, trimming or next-configuration start is involved.
